title: Prove the exact Gaussian-dyadic five-qubit Clifford threshold is 15
body:
The minimum raw tensor width for an exact Gaussian-dyadic left inverse of the full five-qubit Clifford alphabet is **15**. #7806 established a complex kernel at 14 and complex independence at 15. #7803 gave the previous dyadic upper bound of 17. This result closes the gap by proving that the seven-pair subgroup average generates the whole symplectic group algebra over the Gaussian dyadics.

At primes 5, 7, 11, 17 and 31, every one of 931 modular irreducibles has a fixed vector. Characteristic 3 requires a different argument. Restricting a hypothetical obstruction to two orthogonal subgroups forces its normalized trace at the same involution to equal both −1/31 and −67/1309. Ordinary characters handle the other primes. Reduction at all maximal ideals then proves existence of the integral splitting. The same data prove a quantitative bound: at least 6/6919 of the dimension of every finite-dimensional module in odd characteristic is fixed by the seed. Constructing a small circuit and pricing its extraction remain open.

Two independent computations reproduced all **1,005** modular character triples, using native GAP/CTblLib and the published Modular Atlas decomposition matrices. A separate binary-space check verifies the subgroup embeddings and the original class fusions. The contribution builds on the Bell interpolation and complex threshold in #7803 and #7806, the prior Clifford work of alephnan and Ali Romman, and the ATLAS, Modular Atlas and GAP character-table contributors. The selected multiplication bound is unchanged.

All four registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and from the read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The repository checks also verified committed bytes, source history, file modes and the export inventory.
